about: Build queue. Work the 'ready' items top to bottom without re-asking the owner; they are decided. 'blocked' items wait on what 'blocked_on' says. When an item is done, delete it here and add a 'done' entry to progress.json (replacing its 'planned' entry if it has one).

items.title: Mortal units, fallen heroes
items.decided: Owner, 2026-10-07: units are mortal; heroes fall and can be revived.
spec: Basic troops and workers (every role except CAPTAIN, CHAMPION, BEAST) die for good, as now.

Player-owned Captains, Champions and war beasts don't die: at lethal damage they fall instead (cancel the death, health to 1, a FALLEN state synced to the client so they lie down; raiders' heroes still die).
While fallen: no AI or attacks, untargetable by enemies, can't be hurt; the owner sees a chat line saying where it fell. Window: 60 seconds (config).
Owner right-clicks a fallen hero within the window: it gets up at 50% health, with a short sound and particle cue.

Window runs out: the hero leaves the world and goes on its owner's 'returning heroes' list (a player attachment: role, race, tier, ready time). After 5 minutes (config) the owner can re-summon it at any of their altars for 50% of its mana cost; the altar menu shows returning heroes with a countdown.
Returning heroes still count toward beastLimit and the army cap, so they can't be dodged by letting heroes fall.

Game tests: a Champion at lethal damage falls instead of dying; a fallen hero is revived by its owner at half health; an expired hero lands on the returning list and is summoned at half cost; a Footman still dies.

items.title: Rank ladder: bigger Captains and Champions
items.decided: Owner, 2026-10-07: sizes follow rank, not role.
spec: In SoldierEntity's attribute setup, add a 'captain_scale' SCALE modifier of +0.15 (ADD_MULTIPLIED_BASE) for the CAPTAIN role, on top of unit_scale and race size.
Set champion_scale to +0.30 for every race except the Hive (keeps +0.35). Today it is 0.10 (0.15 orc/dwarf), so most Champions grow.
Other roles: no change. Warlord scale (0.45) unchanged.
Applies to raider heroes too, so enemy Captains and Champions are easy to spot.
Game test: a Captain's SCALE attribute is 1.15× a same-race soldier's, a Champion's 1.30×.
Render a race lineup (soldier, Captain, Champion) for the Codex.

items.title: Demon hellknights: Hellguard, Fiend, Archfiend, Hellknight, Blood Witch
spec: Generated in mods/warfront/tools/units.py like the imps, on the demon rig (no wings).
Shared look: faceless black-iron plate; horns breaking through the helm; digitigrade legs ending in hooves; emissive ember-orange in the visor slit and plate seams.
Hellguard: heaviest plate + tower shield. Fiend: plate + blade. Archfiend (Captain): crest or banner, cape. Hellknight (Champion): most ornate, bigger horns. Sizes from the rank ladder.
Blood Witch (healer): blood-red robes over light pauldrons, horned hood, no full plate.
Render the five beside a Black Legion soldier to prove they read as demons; set designs.json status to review.
items.decided: Owner, 2026-10-07: armored hellknights with horns, hooves and ember seams; Blood Witch robed over light plate.

items.title: Siege outposts and the raid chest
spec: Every 5th siege wave at a War Standard (5, 10, 15...) raises an outpost of the attacking NpcFaction 30 to 50 blocks from the standard, on solid ground, out of the base's tower reach where possible. Make the interval a config (default 5).
While the outpost stands the wave can't be won: the standard's wave-won check waits on it, and the siege bar or chat says 'Destroy the enemy outpost'.

Size scales with the wave: below wave 10, a watchtower camp (palisade ring, tent, wooden watchtower, campfire, about 11x11); from wave 10, a small fort (stone or faction-material walls, gate, two corner towers, about 17x17). Built from structure templates per faction palette; record every placed block so the outpost can be removed cleanly.
Pressure: the outpost sends a small group of its faction's raiders at the base every 90 seconds (config) until taken. It has a few guards of its own.

Raid chest: a new large block entity (2x2 footprint or a big single-block model) at the outpost's heart, with one look per NpcFaction: Marauder war crate, Black Legion strongbox, Burning Horde bone chest, Swarm chitin pod, Silverwood root-bound coffer, Ironbeard vault, Fallen Host reliquary. Holds loot scaled to the wave (loot table per faction). Can't be broken while it still holds items; once empty, breaking it despawns the whole outpost (all recorded blocks and remaining outpost raiders) with a sound and particles, and the wave can then be won.
If the siege ends some other way (the standard is lost or removed), the outpost despawns after a short delay so no ruins are left behind.

Game tests: an outpost spawns on wave 5 and not on wave 4; the wave can't be won while the chest stands; breaking the empty chest removes every outpost block; the chest can't be broken while it holds loot.
Models: render all seven chests side by side for the Codex before calling it done.

items.title: Orc flight: the rocket pack
items.decided: Owner, 2026-10-07: fuel-burst rocket, not long-haul flight.
spec: Chest-slot item, orc only. Hold jump in the air to thrust: upward when looking level or up, forward-and-up when looking down the sprint direction. Strong acceleration, capped speed.

Burns fuel fast: about 3 seconds of thrust per coal/charcoal, about 8 per Mana Crystal (config). Fuel sits in the pack (right-click with fuel to load, tooltip shows seconds left). Empty pack = falls like normal.
Loud and visible: smoke and flame particles plus a rocket sound while thrusting, so enemies hear orcs coming.
Landing from a dive within a second of thrusting does a small knockback shockwave and cancels the orc's fall damage; no damage to blocks.
Placeholder look: a plain iron-and-copper pack on the back with two exhausts (generated, like the glider model); the real design waits on orc player references.
Same pattern as the Mana Glider (flight/ManaGliderItem.java): race-locked, chest-slot or ability as noted, vanilla attributes/effects where possible, a game test for the race lock and the cost.

items.title: Angel flight: wings that fly by day and glide by night
items.decided: Owner, 2026-10-07: free flight by day, elytra glide at night or underground.
spec: Angel players get wings (chest-slot item until the angel player model has built-in wings). Daytime with open sky above (world can see sky at the player's position, not raining hard): creative-style free flight (mayfly), with a slower top speed than creative.
Night, underground, or no sky: flight shuts off and the wings act as an elytra glide only. Switching mid-air drops the player into the glide, never a straight fall.
Crafting: the fallback vanilla recipe now (feathers, Mana Crystals, gold); the Aether recipe from the crossover item replaces it when the Aether is loaded.
Placeholder look: plain white feathered wings from a generated model; the real look waits on the angel player references.
Game test: an angel with wings can fly in daylight with sky and can't (glide only) under a roof.
Same pattern as the Mana Glider (flight/ManaGliderItem.java): race-locked, chest-slot or ability as noted, vanilla attributes/effects where possible, a game test for the race lock and the cost.

items.title: Elf flight: levitate and wind leap spells
items.decided: Owner, 2026-10-07: spell flight paid with Iron's Spells mana.
spec: Two elf-only spells. Levitate: hover and drift slowly while held, a steady mana drain. Wind Leap: a burst launch in the look direction plus slow fall until landing, one cost per cast.
With Iron's Spells loaded: register them as Iron's Spells spells (elf school or nature), paid from Iron's mana, on spell scrolls/ink like the mod's own.
Without Iron's Spells: a Wind Charm item (elf only) casts them, paid with Mana Shards from the inventory. Warfront must load and pass tests without Iron's Spells.
Leaf and wind particles; no wings, no gear on the back.
Same pattern as the Mana Glider (flight/ManaGliderItem.java): race-locked, chest-slot or ability as noted, vanilla attributes/effects where possible, a game test for the race lock and the cost.

items.title: Crossover: homelands and mana fuel
items.decided: Owner, 2026-10-07: replace Twilight Forest with The Aether and Deeper and Darker, and cross them over with Warfront (all four crossovers).
spec: Optional integration like Iron's Spells: check ModList.isLoaded and use tags/registry lookups by id, no hard dependency; Warfront must still load and pass tests without either mod.

Homelands: angels get the race's 'home' bonus in the Aether dimension (aether:the_aether) and the Hive gets its underground bonus everywhere in the Otherside (deeperdarker:otherside), sunlight weakness never applies there. Add a dimension check next to the existing Hive underground logic.
Raids: Fallen Host warbands spawn freely in the Aether, Swarm warbands in the Otherside (NpcFaction homeland predicates take the dimension too). Overworld sieges are unchanged.

Mana: new item tags warfront:mana_fuel/shard_grade and crystal_grade, filled optionally with Aether Ambrosium Shard (shard grade) and Zanite Gemstone (crystal grade), and Deeper and Darker sculk bone / echo-type materials (pick real item ids from the mod's registry at build time). Mana Wells accept anything in the tags. Use tag entries with required:false so missing mods are fine.
Game tests can't load the other mods: test the tag path with a vanilla item added to the tag in a test datapack, and the dimension check via a helper.
